exercises.title: Basic Operations with Vectors
exercises.description:
Given are the vectors $\vec{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$.

a) Calculate $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$
b) Calculate $3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}$
c) Determine the length of $\vec{a}$
solutionSteps:
Step 4: Calculate length of $\vec{a}$
$|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2}$
$|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-1)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 9} = \sqrt{14}$

Step 5: Final results
a) $\vec{a} + \vec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$
b) $3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -11 \\ 13 \end{pmatrix}$
c) $|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{14}$

exercises.title: Dot Product and Angle
exercises.description:
Given are the vectors $\vec{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$.

a) Calculate the dot product $\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}$
b) Determine the angle between the vectors
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Calculate dot product
$\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = u_1 \cdot v_1 + u_2 \cdot v_2 + u_3 \cdot v_3$
$\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = 3 \cdot 1 + 4 \cdot 2 + 0 \cdot 5 = 3 + 8 + 0 = 11$

exercises.title: Simple Linear System
exercises.description:
Solve the following linear system using Gaussian elimination:
$\begin{align}
x + 2y - z &= 3 \\
2x - y + z &= 1 \\
3x + y + 2z &= 11
\end{align}$
solutionSteps:
Step 4: Back substitution - determine z
From row 3: $2z = 7 \Rightarrow z = \frac{7}{2}$

Step 7: Solution
$x = \frac{3}{10}$, $y = \frac{31}{10}$, $z = \frac{7}{2}$
Verification: Substituting into the original equations confirms the solution.

exercises.title: Matrix Operations
exercises.description:
Given are the matrices $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

a) Calculate $A + B$
b) Calculate $A \cdot B$
c) Determine $\det(A)$
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Matrix addition
$A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$
Element-wise addition:
$A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 1+2 & 2+1 \\ 3+0 & 4+3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$

Step 2: Matrix multiplication
$A \cdot B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$
Element (1,1): $1 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 0 = 2$
Element (1,2): $1 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 3 = 7$
Element (2,1): $3 \cdot 2 + 4 \cdot 0 = 6$
Element (2,2): $3 \cdot 1 + 4 \cdot 3 = 15$

Step 4: Calculate determinant
For a 2×2 matrix $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$, $\det = ad - bc$
$\det(A) = 1 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 3 = 4 - 6 = -2$

Step 5: Final results
a) $A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$
b) $A \cdot B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 7 \\ 6 & 15 \end{pmatrix}$
c) $\det(A) = -2$

exercises.title: Linear Independence of Vectors
exercises.description: Check whether the vectors $\vec{v_1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$, $\vec{v_2} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{v_3} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$ are linearly independent.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Approach for linear independence
The vectors are linearly independent if the equation
$\alpha_1 \vec{v_1} + \alpha_2 \vec{v_2} + \alpha_3 \vec{v_3} = \vec{0}$
has only the trivial solution $\alpha_1 = \alpha_2 = \alpha_3 = 0$.

Step 2: Set up system of equations
$\alpha_1 \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \alpha_2 \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \alpha_3 \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$

This leads to:
$\begin{align}
\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \alpha_3 &= 0 \\
2\alpha_1 + \alpha_2 - \alpha_3 &= 0 \\
\alpha_1 + 0\alpha_2 - \alpha_3 &= 0
\end{align}$

Step 5: Back substitution
From row 2: $\alpha_2 + \alpha_3 = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha_2 = -\alpha_3$
From row 1: $\alpha_1 + 2\alpha_2 + \alpha_3 = 0$
$\alpha_1 + 2(-\alpha_3) + \alpha_3 = 0$
$\alpha_1 - \alpha_3 = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha_1 = \alpha_3$

Step 6: Conclusion
The system has infinitely many solutions with $\alpha_3$ as a free parameter:
$\alpha_1 = \alpha_3$, $\alpha_2 = -\alpha_3$, $\alpha_3$ arbitrary

Since there are non-trivial solutions (e.g., $\alpha_1 = 1, \alpha_2 = -1, \alpha_3 = 1$), the vectors are linearly dependent.

Answer: The vectors are linearly dependent.

exercises.title: Inverse of a 2×2 Matrix
exercises.description: Determine the inverse of the matrix $C = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, if it exists.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Calculate determinant
$\det(C) = 3 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 2 = 3 - 2 = 1$
Since $\det(C) \neq 0$, the inverse exists.

Step 2: Formula for 2×2 inverse
For $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$, the inverse is:
$\frac{1}{ad-bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$

Step 5: Final result
$C^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$
The verification confirms the result.
